title: Why I Moved My Index Funds (Fidelity vs Vanguard vs Schwab)
creator: Ana Petrovic
description:
After eight years at one brokerage I moved everything. Here's the boring, honest reasoning: fees, fund options, the app, and customer service when something went wrong.

Nothing in this video is financial advice. I'm a teacher who reads too many fund prospectuses, not a planner.

sentences.t: So in August I moved about eight years of index fund investing from one brokerage to another.
And a lot of you asked why, so this is the very unglamorous explanation.
Quick background, I'm a high school teacher, I put money in every month, and I mostly leave it alone.
I was at Vanguard the whole time, and for most of those years I had zero complaints.
Let's start with fees, because that's what everyone thinks this is going to be about.
And honestly, between Fidelity, Vanguard and Schwab, the fees on a basic total market fund are basically nothing.
We're talking a few hundredths of a percent, on my balance that's the price of a sandwich a year.
So no, I didn't move to save money on fees, the difference was too small to matter.
Funds next, and this is a little more interesting.
All three have a cheap total market fund, a cheap international fund, and a bond fund, which is all I really use.
Fidelity has a few funds with literally zero expense ratio, which sounds amazing but has a catch.
You can only hold those particular funds at Fidelity, so if you ever leave, you have to sell them first.
That's not a dealbreaker, it's just something nobody mentions until you're trying to leave.
Now the app, which is where my frustration really started.
Vanguard's website was redesigned last year, and I could not find my tax documents for three weeks.
I'm not exaggerating, I had my accountant on the phone and I was clicking through menus like it was a maze.
Schwab's app is clean, everything's where you'd expect it, it feels like someone actually tested it.
Fidelity's app is busy but fast, there's a lot on the screen, but I could always find what I needed.
And then customer service, which ended up being the actual reason I moved.
A transfer from my old work retirement account got stuck for six weeks at Vanguard.
I called four times and talked to four people who each told me something different.
When I tested Schwab with a small account, I got a person in under two minutes, and she fixed a problem in one call.
So, Schwab, that's where everything is now.
Okay, before I wrap up, there's one thing I want to be really clear about.
This video isn't sponsored, and none of these three companies has ever paid me for anything.
Brokerages do reach out to sponsor this channel, Robinhood has asked twice, and I've said no both times.
There are no referral links below, nobody saw this before it went up, and I don't get a bonus for moving my money.
I just think you deserve to know that, especially in a video about where to put your savings.
So, where I landed.
If you're happy where you are, honestly, stay, all three are fine for a boring index investor.
Moving took me about three weeks of paperwork and one very long phone call, it's not nothing.
But if something keeps going wrong and nobody can fix it, that's when it's worth the hassle.
Let me know in the comments if you've had a transfer horror story, I genuinely want to hear I'm not the only one.
Thanks for watching, see you next month for the dividend video nobody asked for.
